Check149_114_n01: an explicit S3/A3 computation confirms that an inner automorphism of an ambient group can induce an outer automorphism of a normal subgroup: conjugation by a transposition inverts the generator of A3, whose own inner automorphisms are all identity. This explains a possible group-theoretic obstruction behind the distinction on scans113–114. It does not verify the manuscript’s geometric identification or the claimed ambiguity for the E groups. Check149_114_n02 separately checks only that ambient conjugation restricts to an automorphism when normality is assumed.

checks.outcome: Only the local group-theoretic implication behind the opening wording was checked: for a normal subgroup N of G, conjugation n -> gng^{-1} maps N to N and has inverse conjugation by g^{-1}, hence is an automorphism of N. This page alone does not establish the needed normal-subgroup premise for the E groups, and this check was not used to reconstruct the cancelled indices.

checks.outcome: Exhaustive finite permutation computation in scripts/check_relative_outer_action.py (result review/math/149_scan114_outer_action.json): N=A3 is normal in G=S3; conjugation by (01) sends a=(012) to a inverse. This checks the elementary obstruction behind the discussion of ambient inner action; it does not verify the geometric identifications or existence of the particular ambiguities claimed in the manuscript.
